metadata.title: What's a prompt, really?
metadata.topic: CLAUDE BASICS · WHAT IS A PROMPT
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: what is a prompt? Lands the carry-out that a prompt is everything the model can see — not just what you typed.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B08 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: B09 — context window limits and message dropping

beats.narration_text: Someone started this question as if it were about commands — crossed out command, and wrote prompt instead. What's a prompt, really? Let's find out.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types naive question with 'command', hesitates, corrects to 'prompt', lands the real question

props.text:
What's a command, really?
Is it just
what you type?
What's a prompt, really?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Writer types naive framing with 'command', hesitates, corrects to 'prompt', lands the real question. Liam reads the corrected version over the typing animation.

beats.narration_text: The phrase "write a better prompt" is everywhere. It's good advice — but most people have never stopped to ask what a prompt actually is. The answer changes what the advice means.

shot.new_visual_element: Write a better prompt — but what IS a prompt?

production_viz.label: write a better prompt — but what is it?
production_viz.mechanic: Large serif text 'write a better prompt.' centered at top. Below, in smaller italic: '— but what IS a prompt?' One teal underline rule beneath the main phrase. The question mark is the teal accent.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one picture: you open Claude, type three words — explain DNA — and press Enter. That's the moment we'll come back to.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — 'explain DNA' three words, send arrow

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — explain DNA
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Small teal label 'your message:' above. Large bold 'explain DNA' centered. A crimson dot to the right (send button). Small label below: 'we'll come back to this.' THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B08.

beats.narration_text: The natural read is that those three words are the prompt. You typed them, the AI reads them, works from them — the way a search query is exactly what you typed.

production_viz.label: explain DNA = THE PROMPT — the natural reading
production_viz.mechanic: Left: 'explain DNA' in serif INK. Arrow pointing right. Right: large 'THE PROMPT' in bold INK. Below: italic 'the natural reading' in smaller INK. No crimson — sell this as reasonable. One teal accent on the arrow.

beats.narration_text: But if that were true, Claude would forget what you said last turn the moment you started a new message. It doesn't. Something is being carried forward that isn't just your latest words.

shot.new_visual_element: Conversation carries forward — breaks the naive model

production_viz.label: carried forward — breaks the naive model
production_viz.mechanic: Short conversation thread: Turn 1 (small ink), Turn 2 (small ink). Then 'New message →'. An arrow from 'New message' tries to go only to 'NEW' but connects back to Turn 1 in teal — carried forward. A crimson strike through the label 'only this message'.

beats.narration_text: A prompt is the entire block of text assembled and handed to the model before it produces a single word — not just your message, everything the model can see.

production_viz.label: THE PROMPT — the whole assembled block
production_viz.mechanic: Bold large 'THE PROMPT' at top in INK. Below: a large filled rectangle representing the assembled text block. Inside the rectangle: 'everything the model can see' in smaller ink. One teal bracket around the whole block.

beats.narration_text: It has three parts: system instructions — usually invisible, set by whoever built the interface you're using. The conversation history — every prior exchange, written out in order. And your new message.

shot.new_visual_element: Three stacked sections: SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS / CONVERSATION HISTORY / YOUR MESSAGE

production_viz.label: Three parts of the prompt
production_viz.mechanic: Three stacked horizontal bands, each labeled. Top: 'SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS' in teal. Middle: 'CONVERSATION HISTORY' in ink. Bottom: 'YOUR MESSAGE' in bold ink. Teal left-border rule on the top band. Each band fades in top-to-bottom.

beats.narration_text: All three get assembled, in that order, into one long block. The model reads it from the top, then generates what comes next.

shot.new_visual_element: Three sections collapse into one block → MODEL → GENERATE

production_viz.label: Assembled into one block → model reads → generates
production_viz.mechanic: Left: three small labeled stacked boxes (SYSTEM / HISTORY / MESSAGE). Center arrow. Right: one large block labeled 'PROMPT'. Another arrow to 'MODEL'. Teal arrow from MODEL to 'GENERATE →'. Simple left-to-right flow.

beats.narration_text: Back to explain DNA. In a clean session, the model receives any system instructions — possibly empty — then your three words. It reads the whole block before writing the first word of its reply.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — explain DNA inside the three-part block

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — explain DNA in context
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS: same teal 'your message:' label, same large bold 'explain DNA', same crimson send dot. But now a teal band appears above it: 'SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS: [empty]'. The whole assembly is shown as a block before the model generates.

beats.narration_text: One flag: there's a hard limit on how much the model can hold at once — the context window. When a conversation hits that limit, the oldest messages are quietly dropped from the block. The rest still holds.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — context window limit, oldest messages dropped

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — context window limit
production_viz.mechanic: A tall stack of conversation turns. A horizontal ceiling line labeled 'CONTEXT WINDOW' in teal. The oldest turn at the bottom drops away in crimson. A single teal 'FLAG' label in the top-left corner — the reel's only hedge, labeled as one.

beats.narration_text: So a longer conversation doesn't mean the model remembers more. Hit the context limit and the oldest part of the conversation drops — automatically, without notice.

shot.new_visual_element: DIRECTION A — longer conversation, no more memory

production_viz.label: DIRECTION A — longer conversation ≠ more memory
production_viz.mechanic: Top: 'LONGER CONVERSATION' → arrow → 'REMEMBERS MORE' — arrow struck through with crimson. Below: short label 'oldest turns dropped at the limit' in INK. The strikethrough is the only crimson.

beats.narration_text: And a short message doesn't mean a small context. A developer might have loaded the interface with a long set of instructions. Those arrive silently at the top of every block, before your first word.

shot.new_visual_element: DIRECTION B — short message, large hidden context

production_viz.label: DIRECTION B — short message ≠ small context
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring B10: 'SHORT MESSAGE' → arrow → 'SMALL CONTEXT' — struck through crimson. Above the message: a large teal block labeled 'SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS (hidden)' — looming larger than the user message. Same layout as B10, opposite meaning.

beats.narration_text: A prompt is everything the model can see — not just what you typed, but the whole conversation and any instructions that were set before you arrived.

props.quote: A prompt is everything the model can see — not just what you typed, but the whole conversation and any instructions that were set before you arrived.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: before you answer anything else, walk me through what's in your context right now. Everything you can see — any instructions you were given, the conversation so far, my current message. What does the full picture look like from your side? Run that today. You'll see the three parts arrive in the order they were assembled. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Before you answer anything else, walk me through what's in your context right now. Everything you can see — any instructions you were given, the conversation so far, my current message. What does the full picture look like from your side?

beats.narration_text: What's a prompt, really? Liam, in for Bear.
